title: Introduce lightweight RAG local-orchestrator playbook and tool-caller examples
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new local RAG playbook and compact tool-calling examples aimed at low-friction developer onboarding. No breaking changes. Quickstart contains run instructions and suggested eval prompts.
description:
Motivation: Provide a compact, battery-included local "playbook" that demonstrates an orchestrator pattern for RAG workflows (retrieval -> agent decision -> tool-calling -> synthesis) without requiring full infra. This is targeted at engineers who want to prototype multi-tool agents and iterate on prompt/tool interfaces locally before deploying to Redwood Dedicated or Private.

What this PR includes: checklist and quick runnotes:
- Add a small local orchestrator (Node + minimal worker) that demonstrates: document index loading, candidate retrieval, a simple policy layer, tool-calling (HTTP webhook / local function), and final answer composition.
- Two tool-caller examples: (1) fact-check HTTP tool that queries a pre-bundled knowledge stub, (2) calculator function demonstrating structured tool calling and typed JSON inputs.
- A focused quickstart doc (docs/LOCAL_ORCH_README.md) with steps to run the example, test prompts, and suggestions for integrating with Redwood SDKs.
- CI smoke tests: small e2e that runs the orchestrator in-process and asserts end-to-end expected signals (fetch -> tool -> synth).
- Example prompt set and eval harness hooks for Redwood Optimize (simple regression checks).

Quickstart highlights and commands (also in docs/LOCAL_ORCH_README.md):
1) npm ci && npm run build:local-orch
2) npm run local-orch:start -- which spins up the orchestrator and a mock tool server on localhost:4001
3) npm run local-orch:test to run the smoke scenario (will run the retrieval, trigger tool calls, and assert the final structured output).

Design notes and compatibility: this playbook intentionally avoids heavy dependencies: the retriever is a tiny in-memory FAISS-like stub (vector store shim) and the orchestrator uses Redwood SDK-compatible request shapes so users can swap in real endpoints later. The tool-calling examples use the same JSON schema that the Redwood API uses for function/tool-calls so the transition to hosted/private is straightforward.

Summary of commits:
- add: local-orch/ (orchestrator runtime, small CLI)
- add: local-orch/tools/ (http-tool, calculator)
- add: docs/LOCAL_ORCH_README.md (quickstart + testing notes)
- add: examples/local-orch/prompts.json (seed prompts + evals)
- ci: add lightweight smoke job to quickstarts CI matrix
- test: add e2e smoke harness and fixture data

Changed areas (high level):
- quickstarts/local-orch/ - new orchestrator sample and tool stubs
- docs/LOCAL_ORCH_README.md - new focused quickstart doc with run, test, and extend guidance
- .github/workflows/quickstarts-smoke.yml - extend matrix to run the local-orch smoke check on PRs

Review conversation (high-level timeline):
- Liam: "Nice compact example — can we make the tool schema match the SDK's ToolCall V1 exactly? Also prefer fewer default env variables so it runs out-of-the-box."
- Maya (author): "Updated tool schema to align with SDK ToolCall V1 and defaulted envs to sensible local ports. Added a short compatibility note in the README."
- Priya: "CI looks good but add one assertion that the orchestrator attaches metadata (request_id) to each tool call for traceability."
- Maya: "Added request_id propagation and unit test; pushed new commit."
- Diego: "Approach LGTM; please squash the CI fixup commit into the feature commit when merging."

CI summary: initial matrix had lint warnings on tsconfig (fixed), one flaky test in CI that timed out (rerun), final status: all checks passed. The smoke job runs in ~18s on our runners.

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge to main after approvals from Priya and Diego. Branch deleted on merge.

Notes for maintainers: The quickstart is intentionally self-contained and uses small fixture data. If we want this evaluated as an official sample on docs.redwood.ai, follow-up PR should add a short video gif and an interactive CodeSandbox link (see TODO in README).
